Last block is endurance and it is pretty straight forward. You have fixed pushes and bases of a minute. Four pushes and then the last all out to finishe up the tread blocks. Good distance this morning of 5.54km (3.44 miles). \

First block on the floor is strength and you have a 200m buy-in at a stroke rate of 20 to 24 strokes / minute. From here you have good mornings with a single dumbbell, chest flys and then a lean back with a twist (no dumbbell). \

The next block is a bit of a brute. You are basically doing cleans to push presses in time with the treads. First round is a minute long to count your reps. The recovery is a lateral shift to windmill for a minute. Next round is 45 seconds where you will be expected to keep within a certain number of reps of the clean to push press (coach was saying around 5), another minute of the windmills before the last round of 30 seconds. \

Last block is endurance where you have a longer, 400m row buy-in before the circuit work of a forward lunge with rotation and alt upright row. Repeat this until the finisher which is a minute of a low plank hold. \

>! We have another one of these lift more templates and it's pretty good! Endurance and power on the treads and floor today. Floor has something new as well.. death by tempo where you will kill your biceps, triceps and chest in endless reps of curls, presses and tricep extensions 💀☠️🪦\

Quite enjoyed the tread blocks today. Felt pretty tough in the six minute runs but then the power blocks gave you a nice break to recharge the legs. Good distance this morning of 5.54km (3.442 miles). \

First endurance block is an absolute killer. You have tempo couplets where you are doing 10 reps of an exercise first, then a 10 second isometric hold and then another 10 reps. The first exercise is bicep curls and then the second is a overhead tricep extension. I would definitely choose a lighter weight here as my arms were burning by the end of this! \

From here you have a choice for the power work. You are either on the rower, mimicking the treads with the 30 second all outs or you are doing endless reps of a single arm snatch and then reverse lunges. The snatches are 2 reps each time and the lunges increase in the rep range by 2 each round. \

I started with a normal push and held a base to push throughout. Good distance this morning of 5.79km (3.6 miles). \

One block on the floor, with clusters of exercises. Two rounds of a goblet sit to stand (always a tough one) and then a bridge. Next round is the bird dog low rows (though our coach let us do normal rows instead) paired with a chest press. Last set of exercises is more focused on your core with the dumbbell taps and the low to high chops. Once done just repeat your favourite exercises. \

Last block is by the rower where you are alternating between arnold presses and all out rows. Goal here is to smash out the rows and get your highest wattage each round. Repeat this until the finisher - a 30 second all out row. \

Treads were pretty tough this morning depending on what you pick for the inclines. The first block not too many splats but pretty much orange the whole way in block 2. I picked a base to push for my paces and that felt tough but not over the top. Good distance this morning of 5.76km (3.58 miles). \

Two blocks on the floor as well - both follow the same pattern. You have four exercises to complete before a 30 second all out row. The exercises start off with 20 reps of hops, 12 reps of a lateral raise, 10 reps of a sumo deadlift into 8 reps of the squat to upward rotation. It kind of felt like a mini ESP - endurance first then strength before the power in the all out row. \

Second block is the same but this time the exercises are forward and backward hops, reverse flys, lateral shifts and then sumo squats to uprright rows before the all out rows. Repeat this until the finisher of either the squat to uprward rotation or an all out row. \

Starting with the tread block, this is all about the pyramid of push effort. Starting with a minute of push followed by a 45 second base recovery. Add 30 seconds each time you go back to the push up to the 3 minute effort. From here you go back down by 30 seconds each round until you get to the last minute of push effort and then this is capped off with a 30 second all out. \

Pretty tough today. I didn't have it in me to increase my pushes at the end and I had to lower my base a little at the start of the recoveries to get my breath back. Good distance this morning of 5.89km (3.66 miles). \

Before you do this though you do have a little push-up challenge. Using the bench, you will do a tricep push-up for 30 seconds. The challenge is to see how many reps you can do in the 30 seconds and see if you can beat this in the second block (most I managed was 31). \

In the first block the exercises start with a seated hammer curl then a tap squat and then the constructed set is the seated hammer curl to stand. Once you have done this then you work your way back down again with the tap squats and then the curls. Two rounds of this and then repeat your favourites until time is called. To be honest, I barely got through one round before time was called so not sure 10 minutes is enough to get through two. \

Next block is similar but this time we have goblet lunges with rotations, full lateral step-up and a constructed exercise of the goblet reverse lunge with rotation into a full step-up. Again I only got through a single round before we had to finish. \

You start off on the floor with a bit of a rep / run block. You are grabbing a couple of dumbbells and doing 6 reps of a squat (dumbbells by your side), bicep curls, front loaded alternating lunges and then uppercuts. From here you hop on to the treadmill for a 2 minute run. Coach didn’t say if we needed a particular pace but I assume that this is supposed to be the active recovery portion of the block so use this as a way to get your heart rate back under control. \

… which is a 10 minute endurance block which is basically a mirror of what you just did on the rower. Fixed bases of 45 seconds with increasing pushes of a minute, 90 seconds, 2 minutes and 2 and a half minutes. This will absolutely test your legs. Good distance this morning over all of 3.85km (2.392 miles). \

Heading back to the floor you have your last 10 minute block of increasing reps. This time you have good mornings, tricep extensions, lateral lunges and bear plank low rows. Your active recovery this time is the cobra with shoulder mobility. This is where you lie on the floor extend up through your back and move your arms from straight in front of you to behind and back again. Made it through four rounds this time. \

On the floor you have your first long block which is basically work and rest rounds interspersed with 150m all out rows. In the first round you have a reverse lunge with a dumbbell in one hand followed by a single arm chest press in a bridge hold on the floor. \
After the row you then have a single arm, single leg deadlift followed by a pullover and another row. Thought this was all pretty doable this morning and I got through two rounds of everything. \

Last block was a bit of a killer. It is a construct block where you are building yourself up to the clean to neutral grip thruster. You start off with a minute of exercises broken into 3 rounds of 20 seconds - clean, then a front squat and then a push press. \
From here you have 30 seconds to rest before you do another minute but this time there are two exercises for 30 seconds - a clean to front squat and then a neutral grip thruster. \

After another little rest you bring it all together for a minute - clean to neutral grip thruster and then straight into your finisher which is a 30 second squat hold. Pretty tough and a nice way to end the template. \

Three blocks on the floor. In the first you are doing unilateral work with the bench - single arm chest press and a single arm high row. After you have done both arms then you do 16 reps of the alternating lateral shift. \

Second block is more of the same but this time you have step-downs with dumbbell and then a single arm single leg step-up into a shift (basically you are shifting your weight onto the leg that is on the bench). Once you have done both sides you are into the push up into alternating low rows. \

Last block is a choice - either a row or reps. The row is pretty simple - 2 minute row into a 30 second all out. On the floor you are doing 30 second timed reps of the step-out squats and high pulls on both sides before the finisher of goblet step-out squats. \

lines: ⁠•	⁠6 - 10 x single dumbbell good morning, rest

Last block is endurance and it is pretty straight forward. You have fixed pushes and bases of a minute. Four pushes and then the last all out to finishe up the tread blocks. Good distance this morning of 5.54km (3.44 miles).

First block on the floor is strength and you have a 200m buy-in at a stroke rate of 20 to 24 strokes / minute. From here you have good mornings with a single dumbbell, chest flys and then a lean back with a twist (no dumbbell).

The next block is a bit of a brute. You are basically doing cleans to push presses in time with the treads. First round is a minute long to count your reps. The recovery is a lateral shift to windmill for a minute. Next round is 45 seconds where you will be expected to keep within a certain number of reps of the clean to push press (coach was saying around 5), another minute of the windmills before the last round of 30 seconds.

Last block is endurance where you have a longer, 400m row buy-in before the circuit work of a forward lunge with rotation and alt upright row. Repeat this until the finisher which is a minute of a low plank hold.

If you are expecting a let up on the floor then I think the only silver lining is that there is no rowing. Block 1 starts with a buy-in of 30 seconds of tricep push-ups using the bench. Didn't do quite as well as last time and the most I achieved was 29. \

Once finished with the push-ups you are then into your construct / deconstruct pyramid. Two rounds of a seated hammer curl, tap squat, hammer curl to stand and then back down to tap squats and the hammer curl. Not sure how OTF expects you to do two full rounds of this, I only managed 1 and a bit.. the curls to stand is particuarly brutal. \

Next block is more of the same but this time we have lunges and step-ups 💀☠️🪦This was pretty nasty as well with the jelly legs from the treadmill. Again, you will have the push-up buy-in to contend with but after that it is two rounds of the lunges with rotation, lateral step-ups, lunge to step-up and then back down again. Didn't make two rounds on this block either before the coach called for time. \

>! Happy enough for a power day after the template yesterday. I thought that this would be ok for a green day but it is actually sneaky hard! There is plenty of walking recovery but you do have these little three minute blocks that will definitely get the heart rate up. Then on the floor you have all the snatches, cleans and marching. \

One big block on the floor where you are doing a series of complex, back-to-back exercises. First is a series of a clean, single arm march in place followed by a snatch. Do first on the right side and then on the left. \
Next complex is a low row (two dumbbells), farmer's march in place (dumbbells down by your side) and then a burpee with a knee drive (using the dumbbells). \

Last block is over by the rower. You have a compound movement with a deadlift to bicep curl paired with a 150m row. Now if you do the weights you will be limited by how much you can bicep curl (which should be less than your deadlift weight). Our coach told us to either pause at the bottom of the deadlift or break up the exercise and have two sets of weight. I just went a bit slower and used my bicep curl weight. Your finisher today is a 30 second all out row. \

>! End of school holidays for the kids and back to school for them today. The struggle is real as they will now have to get up before 11am haha. Struggle is also real for us as we have to deal with a high incline run / row and then neverending reps on the floor. \

Once done with all four rounds you get to tread or row for distance until the coach calls for the finisher - 30 seconds all out on either the treadmill or rower. Good distance this morning making 2.02km on the tread for distance. \

On the floor it isn't too much better. You have two blocks of endurance work. First block has four exercises - incline chest press, seated low row, tap squats and then a 4-point to downward dog. You start with 20 reps and each round (you have 3 of them) you cut 5 reps off the total. As you decrease the reps the expectation is that you will be increasing the weight. \

Second block isn't much better. It is the same format but now the exercises are a tricep extension on the bench (dumbbells in both hands), sumo squats, wide stance bridges and then a sit-up with a knee tuck. Get through the three rounds to reach the bonus which is just more of the same but now 5 reps. \

>! Recovered not too bad after yesterdays little run / row. Today we have little power session. All outs is the focus on the treadmills. On the floor it is all about the strength based rows, strong and stable for the exercises and then core buy-outs with the low planks. \

Last block sees the base cut to a minute and the all outs to 30 seconds. Again, you will be asked to tap up the paces so it should be your fastest / highest all out for the template. Good distance this morning of 5.21km (3.237 miles). \

Now on to the floor. Each floor will have a row buy-in as well as a core buy-out of a low plank. In the first block you will have a 25 stroke row at 20-24 strokes / minute and then a circuit of two exercises - squat to upright row and a TRX single arm squat to low row. I only had enough time to do a single round of the exercises before the buy-out, a minute of  a low plank. \

Next block sees the row cut to 20 strokes. The goal here is to stay within touching distance of the last block. The exercises now is the reverse lunge to shoulder press (RIP legs) and then a forward lunge to y-raise with the TRX. The buy-out this time is only 45 seconds of the low plank. \

Last block is more of the same. This time only a 15 stroke row before the exercises of a torso rotation and then a TRX clutch curl to rotation (starting to feel to core work now!). Your finisher this morning is a 30 second low plank. \

I didn't think today was super easy but then again I didn't walk much of the recoveries. The floor work was reasonably tough after the sprints and the rows with all the lunges and squats. Good to see a bit of focus on the core with the last block and all the low plank buy-outs. I would give today a 2 (🪶🪶) out of 5 for gentleness. !<

>! Hills hills hills this morning. Felt like it should have been a revenge template for a benchmark but we haven't had once recently.. maybe for those who skipped Game Day. Four blocks of incline work at base. Bosu on the floor. They even crammed in a couple of little row efforts and burpees into this template 🪦💀☠️ \

Two blocks on the floor. The first starts with a lazy little 2 minute row for distance. No push efforts here like yesterday, 2 minutes as hard as you can go. Once done here you will then be into a complex of bosu work - push-ups, plank pops and squat to shoulder press. Once are done there, have a breather before doing a split stance low row. Repeat the exercises until you get time for a break. \

Last block sees you starting with the complex - kneeling tricep extensions, low to high chops with hip thrusts and then a forward lunge with torso rotation. You then get to take your complex from block 1 and bring it all together into the full burpee with the bosu (yes that includes the push-up and the bosu shoulder press!). Repeat this until the coach calls you over to finish you off with a repeat of the 2 minute row for distance. Furthest I got today after all the hills was 635m. \

lines: Still a little sore after the benchmark row. We have a ESP, lift more template today. Rowing is completely optional (though I chose rowing instead of burpees).

On the floor you also have three blocks. All of them feature back-to-back supersets. In the first block your supersets are front raise paired with seated reverse flys and then a lateral step over (surprisingly hard with the dumbbells) and a good morning. You then have a choice of either a 300m row or straight leg raises on the bench. \

Second block is your strength block. Here you have alternating bicep curls paired with a tricep extension. Next superset is deadlifts paired with front squats. Your choice of row is either a 200m row at 20-24 strokes a minute or bench seated torso rotations. \

Last block is all about power. Your superset here is high rows paired with power push-ups. Your choice here is either a 100m all out row or burpees with step-ups to knee raises. Here I did choose the row :) No finisher today on the floor. \

Once done with the squat hell you are then doing balance bicep curls (I just did normal curls) and then a choice of an upper body exercise with the TRX or a high plank pull through. Repeat this whole block minus the row until time is called to get back on the treadmill. \

Treadmill block 2 is exactly the same as block 1 but this time they see fit to add an all out at the end. These tread blocks really sneak up to and that push to all out and the all out at the end are really quite nasty! Good distance this morning of 5.78km (3.59 miles). \

The tempo couplet work this time is now a bridge with your shoulders on the bench. 4 reps normal, 4 reps slow and then 4 reps slow with a pause at the bottom. Once done you are then doing a balance overhead tricep extension (again I took the balance bit out) and then a choice of either the chest press using the TRX or palm to elbows (definitely did the chest press). No finisher today, just keep on the reps until time is called. \

On the floor you have 2 blocks. Each block has a 2 and a half minute buy-in of TRX work before a circuit and then a buy-out for a minute. In the first block this TRX work is 30 seconds of a rollout, then 30 seconds of a 11 to 1 o’clock press, rest and then repeat. lines: We have bosu on the floor with back-to-back complexes, burpees and more of the 2 minute row challenges.
* 8 x bosu push-up
* 8 x bosu plank pop
* 8 x bosu squat to shoulder press, rest
* 8 each x split stance single arm reverse grip low row

>! Hills hills hills this morning. Felt like it should have been a revenge template for a benchmark but we haven't had once recently.. maybe for those who skipped Game Day. Four blocks of incline work at base. Bosu on the floor. They even crammed in a couple of little row efforts and burpees into this template 🪦💀☠️ \

Two blocks on the floor. The first starts with a lazy little 2 minute row for distance. No push efforts here like yesterday, 2 minutes as hard as you can go. Once done here you will then be into a complex of bosu work - push-ups, plank pops and squat to shoulder press. Once are done there, have a breather before doing a split stance low row. Repeat the exercises until you get time for a break. \

Last block sees you starting with the complex - kneeling tricep extensions, low to high chops with hip thrusts and then a forward lunge with torso rotation. You then get to take your complex from block 1 and bring it all together into the full burpee with the bosu (yes that includes the push-up and the bosu shoulder press!). Repeat this until the coach calls you over to finish you off with a repeat of the 2 minute row for distance. Furthest I got today after all the hills was 635m. \

Your last tread block doesn't look that hard on paper but the effect of the row block should mean that your legs will be extremely fatigued here. You flip the base and push efforts so now you have 1 minute pushes with only a 30 second base in between. Same 30 second all out at the end. This was a lot tougher but not extremely so.. still doable. Good distance this morning of 4.03km (2.5 miles). \

Now over to the floor. First block is 8 minutes as well and you have three exercises to contend with. Using the low bench you will have alternating step down lunges into a knee drive followed by a high plank single arm low row and finally a pullover. Hardest exercise is the lunge but the rest were all ok. \

Next you have your little metabolic block. Step down squats for 30 seconds. Our coach had has do right side and then left rather than alternating each time. Once you have done two rounds of the step down squats (with minimal rest in between) you are into squat jacks before repeating the whole sequence again. \
Last block is similar to the first but your exercises are now a deadbug on the bench, bicycle presses and chest flys. No finisher today, just keep repeating until the coach calls time. \

Last round is a standalone 3 minute pushes. This was pretty hard today, especially increasing your push paces each round - a lot of orange and red through out the studio. Good distance this morning of 5.74km (3.57 miles). \

I was expecting a bit of an easier floor block after such a difficult tread block but it was definitely not the case! You have a 15 minute block to start with 6 exercises to do back-to-back. Each is a pairing of an upper and lower body exercise. Bridge hold close grip chest presses with a bridge hold, bicep curls paired with a forward lunge and then a shoulder press paired with tap squats. I was in the high greens throughout these exercises. \

With the weights for this I opted to have a few sets of dumbbells nearby and to cycle through them based on the exercise with minimal rest. For example, my chest presses weight is not the same as the bridge and the shoulder press weights is not the same as the squats. \

I also found the close grip chest presses a bit hard to navigate as you also doing a bridge at the same time, it was bit harder to maneuver the weights up compared to just lying on the bench. I ended  up using my thighs a bit to get them into position before doing the bridge. Maybe get the coach to help you get the weights up if you going for a more challenging weight. \
Next block is more endurance work - 12 reps each of a high plank alternating low row, plank pops and then a double crunch. No finisher today - not sure I could have done too much more. \

Three blocks on the floor as well. Each block has a stroke count row buy-in and a low plank core buy-out. \

In the first block you have a 25 stroke row before the circuit of exercises - squat to upright row with dumbbells and then a single arm squat to low row using the strap. A minute of planking will see out the block. \

Second block the row is cut to 20 strokes and then a reverse lunge into a shoulder press using dumbbells (hard!) into a forward lunge to y-raise using the TRX. 45 seconds of planking action to finish. \
Last block reduces the row even more and this time you have a torso rotation paired with a clutch curl to torso rotation using the TRX. Your finisher is the plank again for 30 seconds. \

Goal is really to manage your pace so you can return from the increased incline back to the same pace you had before and get your heart rate to settle. I chose something between base and push and that seemed to work well and got me a good number of splats. Good distance this morning of 5.79km (3.6 miles). \

On the floor you basically have shoulder presses and low rows with a light weight mixed with heavy weights on the squat and lunges. In between these blocks you will be doing 90 seconds of reactive drills where your coach will be calling you to be doing either speed squats, 5-step lateral agility shuffles or quick forward / backward hops. These will definitely get your heart rate up and many of class were getting splats during these drills. \
In the first block you have 5 minutes to work through standard shoulder presses, goblet squats, low rows and reverse lunges. \

Next block, after the reactive drills the exercises change a little. Now your shoulder presses are alternating, you have step-out squats, the low row rows are alternating and just to make it fun, OTF has added a burpee to your reverse lunges 💀☠️🪦\

After another set of reactive drills you have your final weighted block which is now reciprocating shoulder presses, transverse squats, reciprocating low rows (aka the Beyonce row) and then a full burpee (chest to floor push-up) into an an alt reverse lunge. \

Last block is all power. Four all out efforts - 30, 45, 60 and 30 second efforts with only 30 seconds of walking recovery in between. Good distance this morning of 5.5km (3.42 miles) on tired legs. \

First block on the floor is endurance. Back-to-back supersets of a front raise with a seated reverse fly and then lateral step overs in the second. You then have a choice of either a 300m push row or straight leg raises. \

Second block is strength and you have alternating bicep curls paired with a tricep extension (lying down, dumbbell in each arm) and then deadlifts paired with front squats. Then you have the choice of a row or seated torso rotations. \
Last block is all power. High rows with power push-ups on the bench and then a choice of an all out row or the burpee to full step-ups. No finisher today, just repeat this until time is called. \

After this you have the main part of the block which is a take-away circuit. Start with the walking lunges then the alternating low row, double crunch, bent arm lateral raise and the alternating lateral lunge and then each subsequent round you take away the last exercise. By the fourth round you just have the walking lunges and the low row. \

Last block is a bit nasty. 4 rounds of a minute of unilateral complex moves - single arm deadlift, hip hinge swing and then a high pull with power. Two rounds each of right and left arms. This entire block is your finisher which is more than enough. \

Pretty rough - the hills were not fun with a dusty head and the floor block wasn't that easy with lunges, low rows and that little block to finish. I would still give today a 2 (🪶🪶) out of 5 for gentleness. !<

>! Everyone was feeling a bit sore this morning. My glutes and quads are in protest mode. I had forgotten this one was coming up and I felt a bit guilty shooting the coach a dirty look when she cheerily announced that we had a strength template this morning. Hills, bosu, rows and burpees are on the menu this morning. \

Last block is the same as block 4. By now your legs should be completely shot.. just in time for the rowing buy-in for the first floor block! Coach did say that if we felt good we should be upping our paces for the last couple of minutes. I did this as a push (like last time) and was blowing a gasket by the end. Good distance this morning of 5.35km (3.32 miles). \

Your floor block will start with a 2 minute row for distance. Pushed this one hard and managed a 630m effort - a bit harder than the push effort from yesterday. From here you will be into your bosu complex - push-ups, plank pops and squat to shoulder press. Have a little rest before going into the low row. \

Last block sees you doing more of the complex - tricep extensions, low to high chops and a forward lunge with a rotation. Have a little break and now you will need to bring all the movements from the first block complex into a full burpee with the bosu! Repeat this little bundle of joy until it is time for the ~~finisher~~buy-out of another 2 minute row for distance. I couldn't match my first distance and ended on 610m. \

On the floor you will also have 3 blocks. One long block and 2 smaller ones to deal with. The long block has two rounds of 3 exercises - a seated shoulder press, sit to stand with a dumbbell and a bird dog low row. >! Last of the February birthday's in our house today (son and puppy being the others) with my daughter turning 12 - Happy Birthday! Nice little endurance + power template. Billed as a run / row you have two timed endurance tread blocks with a little power row in the middle. Floor pretty much the same with some squat action to break up the endurance floor blocks. \

On to the floor for a work and rest style block. Step down reverse lunges into knee raises, single arm low row in a high plank position and then pullovers. Hardest is probably the lunges but you do get plenty of rest. \

Next is the squat-a-thon block. You have 30 seconds of effort with the same pyramid of rest that you got on the rowers. 30 seconds of step down squats, alterating each side, 2 times over. Then you have squat jacks on the low bench before you do the step down squats again. Last little effort is a repeat of the squat jacks. \
Once done with this you have your last block which is now deadbugs, bicycle presses and a chest fly. This block felt easier than the first which was nice. \

Two blocks on the floor. The first is an add-on block where you are starting with your 12 squats to arnold presses and then each round you are adding another exercise - reverse lunges to squat, reverse fly and finally a 400m row. This is a lot of squatting so I was pretty much done by the end and only just made the 400m row. \

Second block starts with the row and all exercises and takes away the exercises until you are only left with the row at the end. Starting with a 200m row you then have the split squats to uppercut, split squat hold with a bicep curl and the kneeling tricep extension. Exercises are all unilateral so do the right side and then the left. This was a bit easier to get through and I had heaps of time by the end. \

Second block drops an all out but increases the push to 90 seconds. Last block is just a 2 minute push into a 30 second base and then the 30 second all out finisher at the end. Good distance this morning of 3.28km (2.038 miles). \

You will get a bit of time to wipe down and move to the rower where you are basically doing the same as the treadmill. Three blocks where you get a push buy-in before you get 30 seconds to hop off before doing 30 seconds worth of jump squats. \

On the last block it is just a straight 2 minute push row, 30 seconds to get off the rower before doing a 30 second round of squat jumps. Coach was getting us to count reps, the most I managed was 33. \

Lastly we have the floor which is one long block of violence. The block is broken into 3 parts. Each part starts with an add-on buy-in of lateral bounds before going into your exercises. In parts 1 and 2 these exercises are an alternating reverse lunge into a push press, low row to deadlift and then cleans. \

In the last part you will have three types of lateral bounds - 40 seconds of the stick it, 40 seconds of the bound into a hop and then 40 seconds of a bound into a squat jump. Once you have finished with your jumping you then get to rest for 30 seconds before the finisher which is 30 seconds of a neutral grip push press 💀☠️🪦\

The only thing this template didn't have was burpees but it was pretty tough. Not too much rest, maybe just enough on the treads and rower but the floor was pretty much non-stop. We gave today a 2 (🪶🪶) out of 5 for gentleness. !<

One long block on the floor as well. Similar to the treads you have increasing efforts using different weights. 3 rounds to get through of the same exercises - front loaded lateral lunges, high to low rows, cross back lunges and a hammer curl to eccentric bicep curl. First round is light weights, next is moderate and then the last round is as heavy as possible. \
At the end of each round you are faced with a choice - either a 200m all out row or a sumo deadlift to squat. \

At the end of the three rounds you either repeat the last round (lifting as heavy as possible) or row for distance. I think our coach cut our floor block short by 5 minutes (I checked the class clock when he called time) so I was bit surprised that I only just finished round 3 before he was calling us to our finisher which was either a 30 second all out row or a 30 second low plank hold. \

First block you are running 480m / 0.3 miles at an incline of between 3 and 5%. Once you have done your distance, you are stopping your treadmill and doing 10 squats next to it. Keep repeating this until time is called. \
Next block the incline goes up to between 4 and 6% but the distance is now 320m / 0.2 miles. Your exercise between tread work is 10 good mornings. \

Last block sees the incline go to between 5 - 7% and the distance is now 160m / 0.1 miles. Your exercise is now a alternating knee raise with torso rotation. Kind of reminded me of a standing bicycle crunch. \

Moving on to the floor you also have three blocks, each with a slightly different focus. Block 1 is about front of body movement - raising the dumbbells up in front of you for the front raise into hammer curl, front loaded forward lunges and then down on the floor for the chest press. \
Next block is about your back. You have the good mornings with tricep kickbacks, reverse lunges and a pullover. \
Last block is about rotational movements and you have the push press with rotations, swing lunges and seated torso rotations. \

First superset is a step down reverse lunge into a hammer curl followed by box jumps. The box jumps may seem pretty odd given that they are on a low bench, but after the run and the lunges there were about all I could give. \

From here you get 2 minutes to switch to the floor where you are basically mirroring the efforts on the tread. You have three exercises to do in the time allocated - a neutral grip front squat, clean to push press and a push-up to high plank pop. In the first part you are doing 10 reps of each before dropping to the floor and doing a double crunch until the coach calls time. In the next 3 parts all that changes is that the number of reps drops by 2 each time so at the end you are only doing 4 reps. \

I found this very hard. Mainly because I chose a weight that I would normally do a clean to push press. The time challenge of getting all the reps out becomes pretty tough the deeper into the block you go and I barely finished each round. \

Once you are done here you will get 90 seconds to mop yourself off and trudge off to the rower where you are doing your all out rows - 1 minute, 45 seconds and 30 seconds. This should kill your legs for the last tread block which is a mirror of the first one. Good distance this morning of 5.36km (3.33 miles) and I definitely needed all those walking recoveries today. \

Another 2 minutes to get back to the floor and thankfully it is not a repeat of the first block. Now you just have a normal circuit of weighted movements (deadlifts and double crunches) paired with more core / glute exercises of the wide stance bridge (though I added a dumbbell to this one) and the bird dog. Repeat this until the coach calls mercy and you are done. \

lines: Row block with arnold presses, plyometrics block with a little challenge and then more squatting and lunging for the rest of the floor.
* 12 total x alt arnold press
* 10 x pogo hops
* 10 total x alt power skip
* 10 x speed squat
* 5 each x 90 degree pop squat, rest

* 5 each x single arm step out squat, rest

* 5 each x front loaded single arm cross back lunge, rest

You don't head to the floor straight away. You have a rowing block first. Four rounds of decreasing row distances - 200, 150, 100 and 50m at a stroke rate of 22 - 24. In between each row you will be doing alternating arnold presses for 12 reps. Once you finish, hop back on the rower to finish out the block. \

Now you get to the head to the floor but for your plyometric block. Your coach will be asking you to try and get through as many rounds of possible of pogo hops, power skips, speed squats and 90 degree pop squats. I finished 6 rounds and was pretty stuffed by the end. \

Last block is a mix of upper and lower body work. We have kick backs but the grip is supinated so it looks more like a bicep curl grip. Next is single arm step out squats then a compound movement with the bicep curl to wide bicep curl and finally cross back lunges. \

lines: Power focused tread template with load and mobility sets on the floor. We had cleans and push presses the other day and now we have snatches!
* 8 each x goblet split squat
* 8 total x bodyweight alt reverse lunge with t-spine rotation, rest
* 8 each x split stance single arm low row
* 8 total x alt step back low row, rest
* 6 x single arm deadlift (L)
* 6 x single arm snatch (L)
* 6 x single arm deadlift (R)
* 6 x single arm snatch (R), rest
* 5 each x full lateral step-up to knee raise
* 5 each x bodyweight lateral lunge to knee raise with overhead reach, rest
* 8 x bridge hold with close grip bench press (shoulders on bench)
* 5 each x bodyweight single leg downdog to single leg knee drive, rest
* Repeat until **finisher**: 30 sc of alt single arm snatch

Three blocks also on the floor. The first block features back to back sets where you load up first and then pair it with a mobility exercise. First pairing is split squats with a reverse lunge into a t-spine rotation. Second pair is low rows paired with alternating step back low rows (kind of felt like it hit the hamstrings a bit as well). \
Second block is a power block - non stop single arm deadlifts with snatches. Do all reps on the left side before switching over to the right before you get a rest. \

Third block is similar to the first. This time you have full lateral step-ups with a knee raise paired with a bodyweight lateral lunge into a knee raise and overhead reach. Second pairing is a close grip chest press but where you rest your shoulders on the bench and maintain a bridge hold. Pair this with a downdog into a single leg knee drive (just watch out behind you as I almost kicked our coach as he was walking by!). Your finisher today is more of the snatches for 30 seconds. \

>! Ok not cool OTF😒 We have now had hills 2 days in a row. And you seem to be in love with cleans and snatches. Tough run / row today with inclines and some decent endurance runs and then on the floor we have some of these 360 type blocks and then 2 minutes of clean to front squats at the end to absolutely trash your legs. On the plus side it is [Mrs DC](/u/mrsdc031114) and I's 23rd wedding anniversary today so we have a nice dinner planned to celebrate (sans kids :) \

On the floor you start with a real shoulder burner. Front raises into lateral raises into a reverse fly. I used lighter weights for this and the shoulders were absolutely on fire by the end. The next back to back round is back to lunge-theory with forward lunges, lateral shifts and a reverse lunge into calf raises. \

Next block is similar to the first. This time you have some strap work start with with the chest press, single arm side facing bicep curls and then a low row. The next triplet is a farmers march in place (coach said to go heavy!), high to low chops and superheroes on the floor. \

Last block is very nasty. You have 3 rounds of a clean to front squat. Your coach will ask you to count your reps and match or beat that each round. This is pretty tough even with the little 15 seconds of rest in between. \

Start with a minute push into a 3 minute base, next is another 1 minute push into a 2 minute base and then finally it is a minute push into a 90 second base and the minute all out finisher. Each time you go back to base you will be expected to tap it up a little to see if you can still recover. Good distance this morning of 5.62km (3.492 miles). \

In the first block you have a full step-up (dumbbells in both hands), then a bench press into a reach, reverse lunges using the straps to support you and then finally a forward lunge with a y-raise. Repeat this for the whole block (can probably get through this 2-3 times) before you head to the rower for your buy-out, a 1 minute all out row. \

Next block is much the same. This time you have single arm, single leg lateral step-ups, chest flys, a y-raise with the TRX and then a rollout (also using the TRX). Same finisher - 1 minute all out on the rower. \

>! A few sore bodies from yesterday's birthday festivities. My legs have just about recovered from all the rowing and burpees. Today we have a switch template but it is pretty leg heavy again with some serious inclines, tap squats, lunges, and jump squats. \

Move off to the floor before you.. head back to the rower. Your buy-in is a 3 minute build, minute of base, push and all out. From here you properly move back to the floor for back-to-back sets of front tap squats paired with tap jump squats. Take a bit of a break and then move into a pullover with alternating leg extensions. \

You will probably only get through a couple of rounds of the exercises before you get called back to the treadmill. The goal here is to tap up your paces just a little so you can beat your last distance. Good distance this morning of 5.422km (3.37 miles). \

Last block is similar to the first floor block. After your little 3 minute build row you are into upper body work for a change - chest press, power push-ups and then, after a rest, lateral lunges. Continue this until the coach calls you into your finisher - 45 seconds of tap jump squats! \

>! Power day today but unfortunately not a lot of let for your legs, particularly if you decide to do the split squats for your final block. \

In the first block the buy-in is a 30 second push into a minute push and your walking recoveries are all a minute. In the second block the buy-in increases to a 45 second push, 75 second base and you get 75 seconds to walk between all outs. Last block the buy-in is now a minute push into a 90 second base and your walking recoveries are a glorious 90 seconds. Good distance this morning of 5.21km (3.237 miles). \

The first part sees you going heavy with the close chest press for 6 - 10 reps on a nice heavy weight and then drop the weight by a couple of kgs (5-10 lbs) for as many reps as possible. Then move into your back to back movement which is lateral lunges followed by rollouts in to tricep extensions with the TRX. \

At the 8 minute mark your coach will call you straight into part 2. The drop sets are now seated low rows and the back-o-back exercises are a cross back lunge followed by a clutch curls into a torso rotation. \

After this you get a bit of a choice. Bit like choose your favourite poison.. a 5.25 minute row for distance or never ending split squat drop sets. Back leg is on the bench so you can’t use it that much apart from stability so you are going really heavy on that one leg. I did the split squats as I had enough rowing yesterday and for the birthday burn and was kind of regretting by the end. \

>! Nice way to end the week. Word of the day is surge. We have surges in the tread blocks and also on the floor. A bit of power with the 45 second all outs. No lunges or chest press in sight today. On other news, looks like I am coming to Las Vegas in late April - on the lookout for suggestions on studios nearby! \
Coach said that we should start with maybe a pace just under push and the tap up should take us into that orange zone. I went a little bit under the push and went to a push for the minute. \
Next two blocks repeat blocks 1 and 2 so no surprises there. Good distance this morning of 5.51km (3.424 miles). \

First block you have shoulder presses to start and then sumo goblet squats. Once done your 15 reps of these you then do bicycle crunch for 12 reps. Personally, I felt the reps really start to burn around when you are finishing the heavy reps, so the moderate weight straight after was struggle street - shoulders and legs are burning now. \

Once these are over you will have to motor to get back to the floor for the next surge and return set. This time the exercises are a hammer curl and then a sumo deadlift. The core exercise at the end is a back extension on the floor. \

>! Was looking forward to a decent run / row this morning but we have a coach-timed effort here. On the floor we have work and rest with thrusters, lunges, speed skaters and step overs. Your last block is a killer - push press challenge! \

4 x 3 minute pushes on the treadmill and 3 x 2 minute pushes on the rower. Good distance this morning of 3.14km (1.95 miles) - yes I did try and time it so I could get Pi on the tread block haha. Our coach was telling us also to increase the push pace each round but said it was enough to just maintain it. \

On the first block you are starting with a work and rest set of single arm thrusters, step down reverse lunges and alternating low rows. From here you then do some back to back power movements with the speed skaters, step overs and toe taps. \

After all of this you finish with the metabolic block. The goal here is to count all your thruster reps to try and reach a certain goal. Green is 18 reps, Orange is 24 reps and Red is anything over 30 reps. \

You start with the walking lunges for 40 seconds (coach said we could just do forward lunges on the spot) and then 20 seconds to rip out as many thrusters as possible. Repeat this another two times to get your total thruster count. I pushed it (one of the only times I've gotten to red on the floor!) and managed 43 in this block. \

This pattern repeats another 6 times - 30 second all out into a 3 minute walking recovery, getting to base as soon as you feel ready. Thought this was pretty doable today and is a nice change of pace compared to yesterday's run / row. Good distance this morning of 5.38km (3.34 miles). \

Last block on the floor and you have a stability circuit to start - squat to high row with the TRX, a tricep extension and then an alternating single leg airplane (kind of like a single leg deadlift without the dumbbell). \

One round of the stability work and then you are into the strength portion of the floor work. High rows, tricep extensions and a deadlift to carry the pattern over from the stability circuit. Repeat this until the finisher - 30 seconds of tricep push-ups. \

Goal is really to manage your pace so you can return from the increased incline back to the same pace you had before and get your heart rate to settle. I chose something between base and push and that seemed to work well and got me a good number of splats. Good distance this morning of 5.79km (3.6 miles). \

On the floor you basically have shoulder presses and low rows with a light weight mixed with heavy weights on the squat and lunges. In between these blocks you will be doing 90 seconds of reactive drills where your coach will be calling you to be doing either speed squats, 5-step lateral agility shuffles or quick forward / backward hops. These will definitely get your heart rate up and many of class were getting splats during these drills. \
In the first block you have 5 minutes to work through standard shoulder presses, goblet squats, low rows and reverse lunges. \

Next block, after the reactive drills the exercises change a little. Now your shoulder presses are alternating, you have step-out squats, the low row rows are alternating and just to make it fun, OTF has added a burpee to your reverse lunges 💀☠️🪦\

After another set of reactive drills you have your final weighted block which is now reciprocating shoulder presses, transverse squats, reciprocating low rows (aka the Beyonce row) and then a full burpee (chest to floor push-up) into an an alt reverse lunge. \

lines: Last workout before we head off to the coast and it had to be hills.. and burpees.. 😭

We have something different today.. after the “ultimate” hills and “ultimate” burpees your coach will get you to do guided breath work. This is where your coach will be getting you to inhale and exhale on a count to help slow your breathing down and recover better. Didn’t mind it having done breath work in the past.
* 6 each x goblet transverse full step-up
* 10 total x alt chest fly
* 10 total x deadbug, rest
**Floor Block 2 - ultimate burpee construct**
* 30 sec of push-up to alt low row
* 30 sec of neutral grip thruster
* 30 sec of ultimate burpee with neutral grip thruster
* 30 sec of push-up to alt low row
* 30 sec of neutral grip thruster
* 30 sec of ultimate burpee with neutral grip thruster
* 10 total x alt reverse fly
* 10 total x high plank alt superhero, rest

>! It’s like OTF is taking it personally that Mrs DC and I are having a holiday! We have high inclines, ultimate burpees but on the flip side we have some guided breath work on the screens to help try and slow the heart rate down after some decidedly nasty blocks. \

You will get a minute to walk before you go into what the coach called our ultimate hills (I guess to complement the ultimate burpees on the floor??). 30 seconds each of a 10, 12 and 14% incline. Most people are power walking these ones. I guess the only mercy is that they are pretty short. \

On the floor you will have first floor block of 8 minutes. You have a  little 1 minute push row to start before getting into your back to back exercises. This has you doing transverse step-ups, alternating chest flys and dead bugs. I find the alternating chest flys a little challenging given you really have to concentrate to manage the single  dumbbell on the way down as you don’t have the other arm really to help balance it. \
From here you now have your ultimate burpee construct. 30 seconds of push-ups into low rows straight into neutral grip thrusters into ultimate burpees with those neutral grip thrusters ☠️🪦💀 \

Last block is similar to the first. A minute to row up front (try to beat your distance from block 1) before a back to back set of goblet step down toe taps, alternating reverse flys and high plank superheroes. No finisher today, think the burpees were enough. \

Tough template today - nothing at flat road, ultimate burpees will definitely get the heart rate up. I would give today a 1 (🪶) out of 5 for gentleness. Feels like April is over-compensating for having no benchmarks! !<

On the floor you have 2 blocks. The first is a combined strength and endurance block. First part is just over 8 minutes to do a tempo row of 300m before a circuit of a lateral lunge to bicep curl and then a chest press on the bosu with the leg lift. Once the coach calls time for the endurance part you are doing another 300m row and then high rows to deadlifts (a bit annoying given I can deadlift more than I can high rows) and then tricep extensions on the bosu. \

Last block is power and you have another 300m row (lets just call it an all out) followed by more lunges into a press and then a hip thrust on the bosu with a low to high chop. Repeat this until the finisher of full v-ups on the bosu for 30 seconds. \

lines: Row block with arnold presses, plyometrics block with a little challenge and then more squatting and lunging for the rest of the floor.
* 12 total x alt arnold press
* 10 x pogo hops
* 10 total x alt power skip
* 10 x speed squat

* 5 each x front loaded single arm cross back lunge, rest

You start with a row block first up after the trad. Four rounds of decreasing row distances - 200, 150, 100 and 50m at a stroke rate of 22 - 24. In between each row you will be doing alternating arnold presses for 12 reps. Once you finish, hop back on the rower to finish out the block. Pretty tough if you want to get all the rows done. \
Now you get to the head to the floor but for your plyometric block. Pogo hops, skips, squats and pop squats back to back as many times as you can get through. Managed six rounds of these again.  \
Last block has you doing tricep kick backs, curls, step out squats and cross back lunges. Thought this was almost like a recovery block compared to the other two! \

I think the efforts are random, maybe for a minute or so before you return to your original pace. After the all outs the coach let us walk if we needed but the expectation is that you get back to your original pace. You may need to also adjust your effort on the strength blocks given the high incline. Good distance this morning of 5.34km (3.318 miles) on a tough tread block. \

On the floor the ESP theme continues but minus the random efforts. This is a circuit of endurance work (high reps of close grip chest press, step-up to knee raise), strength (pullovers and then a reverse lunge to goblet squat) and power (explosive shoulder presses followed by lateral step-ups with power). Keep this going before heading over to the rower for your finisher block. \

The floor kicks you off with a nasty little shoulder burner, 10 reps of front raises, then lateral raises and finishing with high rows. Next round is front loaded lateral lunges, lateral shifts and then revese lunges into calf raises. \

Second block is more of the same. This time you have strap work with a chest press, single arm bicep curls and a low row. Next round is the farmer's march in place, high to low chops and superheroes. \

Last block is very nasty. 30 second rounds of a clean to front squat (coach was saying to go heavy!!) with only 15 second of rest in between. Count your reps as you will need to try and beat it each round. \

Next rounds follow the same pattern - more time and more incline until the final round of 4 and a half minutes at an incline of 5%. Good distance this morning of 5.18km (3.219 miles). \

First superset is a step down reverse lunge into a hammer curl followed by box jumps. The box jumps may seem pretty odd given that they are on a low bench, but after the run and the lunges there were about all I could give. \

Next superset is a high plank on the low bench into single arm low rows followed by low rows. Last superset is step down squats and then hop overs. Repeat these until you get to your dedicated row block for 4 and a half minutes. By now you shouldn't have that much left in the tank - 1230m was all I could give.. \

Two blocks on the floor. The first is broken into two parts over 16.5 minutes. You are going heavy with a close grip chest press on an incline bench followed by as many reps as possible with a lighter weight. After this you then are doing another back to back set of lateral lunges followed by a TRX move of rollout to tricep extension. \
Second part at the 8 minute mark is more drop sets. Seated low rows and then a cross-back lunge into TRX clutch curls with a torso rotation. \

After all this you get a choice - more drop sets torture or a 5.25 minute row for distance. Only one person took up the rowing today, everyone else did the split squat drop set. Pretty heavy on the legs and definitely feeling this by the end. \

>! It’s like OTF is taking it personally that Mrs DC and I are having a holiday! We have high inclines, ultimate burpees but on the flip side we have some guided breath work on the screens to help try and slow the heart rate down after some decidedly nasty blocks. \

You will get a minute to walk before you go into what the coach called our ultimate hills (I guess to complement the ultimate burpees on the floor??). 30 seconds each of a 10, 12 and 14% incline. Most people are power walking these ones. I guess the only mercy is that they are pretty short. \

On the floor you will have first floor block of 8 minutes. You have a  little 1 minute push row to start before getting into your back to back exercises. This has you doing transverse step-ups, alternating chest flys and dead bugs. I find the alternating chest flys a little challenging given you really have to concentrate to manage the single  dumbbell on the way down as you don’t have the other arm really to help balance it. \
From here you now have your ultimate burpee construct. 30 seconds of push-ups into low rows straight into neutral grip thrusters into ultimate burpees with those neutral grip thrusters ☠️🪦💀 \

Last block is similar to the first. A minute to row up front (try to beat your distance from block 1) before a back to back set of goblet step down toe taps, alternating reverse flys and high plank superheroes. No finisher today, think the burpees were enough. \

Tough template today - nothing at flat road, ultimate burpees will definitely get the heart rate up. I would give today a 1 (🪶) out of 5 for gentleness. Feels like April is over-compensating for having no benchmarks! !<

>! Repeat of the template from last Pi day (3 / 14). Run / row on the treadmills which is pretty hard and then a killer floor block with a lot of lunging, push presses and plyometrics. \
Our coach was asking to try and beat our distance each round but it will be difficult given how heavy your legs will get after the row. Good distance this morning of 3.35km (2.08 miles). \

Your work and rest set has you doing single arm thrusters with a rotation, step down reverse lunges (from a low bench) into a single leg knee drive and then finally an alternating low row. For the plyo exercises it is speed skaters, step overs and toe taps - 12 reps each. You should be able to get through maybe 4 rounds of each. \

After all this you will finish with the metabolic block. This is all back-to-back exercises of walking lunges and push presses. Your goal is to count all the presses and try to get either 18 reps (green), orange (24) and red (30+). \

You will have 40 seconds of walking lunges straight into 20 seconds of push presses. Count the reps on the push presses only as that is what you will be trying to compare at the end. This is pretty hard and you will definitely get splats in this block. \

You start off on the floor with a bit of a rep / run block. You are grabbing a couple of dumbbells and doing 6 reps of a squat (dumbbells by your side), bicep curls, front loaded alternating lunges and then uppercuts. From here you hop on to the treadmill for a 2 minute run. Coach didn’t say if we needed a particular pace but I assume that this is supposed to be the active recovery portion of the block so use this as a way to get your heart rate back under control. \

… which is a 10 minute endurance block which is basically a mirror of what you just did on the rower. Fixed bases of 45 seconds with increasing pushes of a minute, 90 seconds, 2 minutes and 2 and a half minutes. This will absolutely test your legs. Good distance this morning over all of 3.85km (2.392 miles). \

Heading back to the floor you have your last 10 minute block of increasing reps. This time you have good mornings, tricep extensions, lateral lunges and bear plank low rows. Your active recovery this time is the cobra with shoulder mobility. This is where you lie on the floor extend up through your back and move your arms from straight in front of you to behind and back again. Made it through four rounds this time. \

lines: Last workout before we head off to the coast and it had to be hills.. and burpees.. 😭

We have something different today.. after the “ultimate” hills and “ultimate” burpees your coach will get you to do guided breath work. This is where your coach will be getting you to inhale and exhale on a count to help slow your breathing down and recover better. Didn’t mind it having done breath work in the past.
* 6 each x goblet transverse full step-up
* 10 total x alt chest fly
* 10 total x deadbug, rest
**Floor Block 2 - ultimate burpee construct**
* 30 sec of push-up to alt low row
* 30 sec of neutral grip thruster
* 30 sec of ultimate burpee with neutral grip thruster
* 30 sec of push-up to alt low row
* 30 sec of neutral grip thruster
* 30 sec of ultimate burpee with neutral grip thruster
* 10 total x alt reverse fly
* 10 total x high plank alt superhero, rest

>! It’s like OTF is taking it personally that Mrs DC and I are having a holiday! We have high inclines, ultimate burpees but on the flip side we have some guided breath work on the screens to help try and slow the heart rate down after some decidedly nasty blocks. \

You will get a minute to walk before you go into what the coach called our ultimate hills (I guess to complement the ultimate burpees on the floor??). 30 seconds each of a 10, 12 and 14% incline. Most people are power walking these ones. I guess the only mercy is that they are pretty short. \

On the floor you will have first floor block of 8 minutes. You have a  little 1 minute push row to start before getting into your back to back exercises. This has you doing transverse step-ups, alternating chest flys and dead bugs. I find the alternating chest flys a little challenging given you really have to concentrate to manage the single  dumbbell on the way down as you don’t have the other arm really to help balance it. \
From here you now have your ultimate burpee construct. 30 seconds of push-ups into low rows straight into neutral grip thrusters into ultimate burpees with those neutral grip thrusters ☠️🪦💀 \

Last block is similar to the first. A minute to row up front (try to beat your distance from block 1) before a back to back set of goblet step down toe taps, alternating reverse flys and high plank superheroes. No finisher today, think the burpees were enough. \

Tough template today - nothing at flat road, ultimate burpees will definitely get the heart rate up. I would give today a 1 (🪶) out of 5 for gentleness. Feels like April is over-compensating for having no benchmarks! !<

lines: Supersets on the floor with a squat to thruster construct to finish you off.
* 8 x seated low row

Our coach was getting us to increase our paces each round and track our distances both on the treadmill and the rower. I started with a push on the first round and then just increased this each round. On the rower I just aimed to try and get over 400m each row. Good distance this morning of 3.65km (2.27 miles) on the treadmill. \

On the long block you are basically pairing a strength exercise with more of an endurance set with higher reps. First pairing is a low rows paired with cross body bicep curls. Two rounds of this where the goal is to really get to the point of fatigue with the higher reps in the second exercise. \

From here you have deadlifts and lateral lunges (hey it wouldn’t be OTF without a bit of lunging) for 2 rounds. Next set is a sit-up into a sumo squat and then knee tucks. For the sit-up to sumo squat you place the weight at the end of the bench so you pick up at the end of the sit-up and then do the sumo squat. \
If you get through all the rounds then just repeat your favourite until time is called (and why is not the lateral lunges :). \

Instead of a finisher today you just have three minutes of torture. It is a construct block where you start with 10 reps of a seated shoulder press, another 10 reps of a tap squat and then 10 reps of a tap squat into a thruster. From here you only 10 seconds to rest before you do it all over again. This is a real burner and you will likely get into the orange / red for this block. \

From here you get 2 minutes to switch to the floor where you are basically mirroring the efforts on the tread. You have three exercises to do in the time allocated - a neutral grip front squat, clean to push press and a push-up to high plank pop. In the first part you are doing 10 reps of each before dropping to the floor and doing a double crunch until the coach calls time. In the next 3 parts all that changes is that the number of reps drops by 2 each time so at the end you are only doing 4 reps. \

I found this very hard. Mainly because I chose a weight that I would normally do a clean to push press. The time challenge of getting all the reps out becomes pretty tough the deeper into the block you go and I barely finished each round. \

Once you are done here you will get 90 seconds to mop yourself off and trudge off to the rower where you are doing your all out rows - 1 minute, 45 seconds and 30 seconds. This should kill your legs for the last tread block which is a mirror of the first one. Good distance this morning of 5.36km (3.33 miles) and I definitely needed all those walking recoveries today. \

Another 2 minutes to get back to the floor and thankfully it is not a repeat of the first block. Now you just have a normal circuit of weighted movements (deadlifts and double crunches) paired with more core / glute exercises of the wide stance bridge (though I added a dumbbell to this one) and the bird dog. Repeat this until the coach calls mercy and you are done. \

Last block is a repeat of the first and it really doesn't get any better. Good distance this morning of 4.62km (2.87 miles). \

On the floor you have a block of 8 minutes. You start with a minute row at a push pace before doing the back to back exercises. Transverse step ups, alternating chest flys and a deadbug on the bench. \

Second block is the ultimate burpee construct while the treadmill is doing their ultimate hills. Start with the push-up to alternating low row for 30 seconds, then the thrusters and finally the ultimate burpee with the thruster. Coach was saying if you can't do the push-ups on the dumbbells then just do normal push-ups and then grip the dumbbells for the low row. \

Last block is similar to the first but this time you have the all row instead of a push and then the back-to-back exercises of step down toe taps, alternating reverse flys and high plank superheroes. \

Blocks 2 and 4 are the power and are also pretty straight forward. 30 second push, 45 second all out. From here you have a 30 second walking recovery and a 45 second all out, 3 times. Good distance this morning of 4.92km (3.057 miles). \

Four blocks on the floor as well. First and second blocks are the endurance ones. Block 1 sees you doing the reverse grip chest press - kind of like a tricep exercise but you reverse your grip to do the press. You should feel this probably more in the triceps I guess. I chose a lighter weight and it was ok. From there you go immediately into your alternating tricep extensions (lying on the bench). \

Second block is quite a bit harder. Coach was telling us to get a heavy weight for this. You start with a 30 second bridge hold with your dumbbell on your lap, shoulders on the bench and you bridge up through your feet. 30 seconds should be plenty to feel the burn. >! Missed this one while we are at the coast. And when I say missed I didn’t really miss it.. this is pretty horrible. We have more inclines on the treadmill ahead of Everest next week - inclines up to 10%. We have a load of lunging on the floor with bicep curl complexes and snatches. \
Given this is a tread effort you get to pick your speed. I chose to do just over a base at the start and then pared it back for the later rounds. Good distance this morning of 5.02km (3.12 miles). \

Floor isn’t that much better. You have two longish blocks of 8 minutes each that feature a 200m row buy-in at a 20 - 24 strokes / / minute rate. After this you will be on the floor with a single arm reverse lunge followed by a full lateral step-up. First on the right and then the left. Once done you finish off with a bicep curl. Repeat the exercises only until the coach calls time. \
Second block is much like the first. After the row buy-in you are then into reverse lunges with the step-up now and then followed by snatches. Your bicep curls are now wide stance. \

Last block you bring it all together with a horrendous reverse lunge to full lateral step-up to snatch and then the normal bicep curl to wide bicep curl. OTF definitely trying to kill your legs and arms this morning. \

On the floor we also have 3 blocks. The first is a short effort using the mini bands. Slide it in low and in the first round balance on one leg while doing a lateral raise. Second effort is a low band squat into a lateral leg lift. Complete your reps on the right side before moving to the left. \

Your longer block is a mix between endurance and power movements. Start with a step down from the high bench into a hammer curl. Then pick up a weight for single arm snatches. Last exercise is the bench bridge hold with close grip chest press. Round out the block with a minute all out on the rower. \

Last block is more mini band work and I thought this was a bit more challenging. The side plank into a leg lift is pretty hard compared to the high plank toe taps. Repeat this until the finisher of the knee tucks. \

On the floor you have 2 blocks. Each block has a 2 and a half minute buy-in of TRX work before a circuit and then a buy-out for a minute. In the first block this TRX work is 30 seconds of a rollout, then 30 seconds of a 11 to 1 o’clock press, rest and then repeat. No one took up the option to put their feet in the straps! \

Last block is much the same. You have the buy-in of overhead squats + wall slides before a circuit of transverse squats, deadlifts and knee taps. Repeat this until the finisher of knee tucks - either using the straps or not. \

>! Was feeling a bit sore after yesterday's tread effort and the I think maybe the squats. Today is a new month and we have a new set of templates. No Mayhem this month which is a bit disappointing but at least we have the Chipper! Today is endurance on the treads for the most part and then it felt like endurance on the floor as well. \

Last block is a bit of a bonus. You get to choose to either do your all outs on the treadmill or the rower. Pretty much everyone picked the treadmill. 5 30 second all outs with a 30 second recovery in between. Good distance this morning of 5.56km (3.455 miles). \

Over on the floor you have one long floor block before a core finisher. For the long block you are doing back to back exercises - step out squats to reverse lunges paired with low to high chops, then you have lateral lunges to upright rows and double crunches. Last set is chest flys on the floor paired with a bridge. The reps are quite high so you won't have a lot of time to get through multiple rounds. \
Last block is a core finisher. You are doing 2 rounds of 30 seconds each of a superhero, low side plank (each side) and then sit-ups before finishing on a final 30 seconds of a superhero. \

One long block on the floor and then a finisher block. The long block uses the low bench for a load and xplode style circuit. First round is the step down lunges, step down squats and then a little box jump. Second round is the bicycle press, tricep extension and to finish you off with power push-ups. Cap this all off with a 200m all out row. \

If you thought that was bad then the finisher block is worse. You are working high plank alternating knee drives (with your hands on the dumbbells), a short 10 second rest before you go into burpees with alternating low rows. Two rounds of this before you get into your finisher of a final 30 seconds of the high plank altnerating knee drive. \

After all four rounds on the tread you then move on to the floor. Good distance this morning of 5.6km (3.48 miles). \

First block should be 5 minutes and you have a core buy-in to start. 12 double crunches, 12 alternating v-ups and 12 high plank pull throughs. Once done (and you probably won't have a lot of time to do this) you are then into repeating rounds of reverse lunges and bicep curls. The lunges are fixed at 2 reps each and your curls increase by 1 each round. \

From here move to the rower where you have a similar round to the treads. 3 rounds of 90 seconds to complete a 100m all out row and then 6 clean to front squats. Again, our coach went a little rogue and we just did as many rounds as we could for four and a half minutes before the buy-out of the farmers march in place. \
Back to the floor again and you are doing a similar round to the first. You have the same buy-in but this time the exercises on the floor are a reverse lunge and then an upright row. \

Back to the rower for the last block and this is similar to the second block. 3 rounds of 90 seconds to complete a 100m all out row followed by 6 reps of  clen to neutral grip thruster. Again our coach went a little rogue and we were just asked to do as many rounds as possible in the four and a half minutes before the finisher of the farmer's march. \

>! Happy birthday to two of our coaches today. Coach this morning was in a good mood.. he got to give us inclines, more chest press and then some core work in every floor block! \

In between each block you do get a lot of walking recovery as well - 2 minutes. While the tread is billed as strength it really did feel like a power day. Pushes at 8% did suck but luck it was quite short. Good distance this morning of 5.02km (3.12 miles). \

First block is an endurance burner with 12 reps of a close grip chest press, 10 second pause at the top before as many reps as you can manage afterwards. Once done, you can take a rest before you do the power work of a sit-up to squat jump. Repeat this until the last 75 seconds where your coach will take you through a core blast. We did a low plank. \

Second block is similar to the first. This time the endurance effort is a bench bridge. It says to do 2 dumbbells but I just used one heavier dumbbell. Again 12 reps, pause at the top for 10 seconds and then as many reps as you can manage. Your power move this time round is a push-up. Repeat this until the last minute which is another core exercise. \

Last block replaces the exercise with seated hammer curls. Your power movement is the single leg lateral step-up with power - 3 reps each side. Repeat this until the finisher of 45 seconds of a core exercise. \

>! Nice little ESP template today even though there is more lunging (but no chest press!!). We have a few inclines in the strength part but felt reasonably manageable. \
In the endurance part this is a 40 stroke row at a tempo of 1 to 2. Then you have the lateral shifts paired with lateral lunges (definitely not my favourite). \
At the 9 and a half minute mark you will move into the strength part. This will be a 20 stroke row at a 1:3 tempo and then into front squat to shoulder press and then single leg shoulder presses. \
Last part is power. You have a short, 10 stroke row and then split squats and then a split squat hold with a bicep curl. Your finisher today is a 30 second low plank hold. \

>! This definitely felt like a revenge template this morning. We have a mostly endurance template bookended with a few little power blocks. It is supposed to be a lift more template but the choice of doing burpees over rowing didn’t really feel like great trade off.. however most people chose burpees this morning after the rowing yesterday (short that it was). \
Last block on the treads is a repeat of the first effort and then you are done. Good distance this morning of 5.33km (3.312 miles). \

On the floor you actually start with a minute push to all out row. You then get a choice. Either walk back to the floor and do the dreaded dumbbell burpee to squat to press or do another all out row for a minute. I was feeling a bit sore after yesterday so I opted for a slow set of burpees (think I got maybe 15 in the minute - am sure some folks could do that slower). \

Your main block is a takeaway style circuit and is all endurance. Your first round has four exercises - a situp on the bench to a sumo squat, bicep curl to wide bicep curl, transverse step-ups with a dumbbells and then a single arm high row to low row. Once you finish the round you get to do another 3 but each round you get to drop off an exercise of your choosing. I chose to drop the step-ups, then the bicep curls and then the high to low rows. The compound movements really killed my arms this morning and they are still a little bit on fire. \
Last block is the same as the first. More people chose burpees this time (slow burpee reps ftw!) but you also have your choice of your SoS finisher. \

match.line: Your main block is a takeaway style circuit and is all endurance. Your first round has four exercises - a situp on the bench to a sumo squat, bicep curl to wide bicep curl, transverse step-ups with a dumbbells and then a single arm high row to low row. Once you finish the round you get to do another 3 but each round you get to drop off an exercise of your choosing. I chose to drop the step-ups, then the bicep curls and then the high to low rows. The compound movements really killed my arms this morning and they are still a little bit on fire. \

2 blocks on the floor. They both repeat the same pattern. You have a loaded, heavy exercise first, then swap the weights to a moderate weight and then body weight for the end. In the first block you have full lateral step-ups (knee raise added to the last one) before you are doing reciprocating chest press. In the second block the exercises change to single leg deadlifts and the reciprocating rows at the end. Your finisher is either a high plank for a minute or the season of strength finisher. \

Last block felt a bit cruel. Endurance based alternating a 90 second push into a minute base. After the fourth push you then go into a 30 second all out finisher. Good distance this morning of 5.14km (3.19 miles). \

First block sees you do 3, 90 second rounds to complete a TRX low row, high row and then an alternating low row. Once done you get to recover until the next round. After the last round you will have a buy-out of a minute of sit-ups (who said we don't do core anymore?). \

Next block is more of the same but this time the exercises are a bodyweight dynamic cossack squat, lateral shifts and then a speed skater. Like the first block, you have 90 seconds to complete the exercises and at the end of the 3rd round you will also have the minute buy-out of sit-ups. \

The last floor block is your endurance block. This has you doing push-ups into a high side plank, pullovers (on the floor) with an alternating leg extension and then finally a single arm stand from a tall kneeling position. Repeat this until finisher of a minute of sit-ups with a knee tuck or your season of strength finisher. \

Thought the tread blocks were pretty tough today - plenty of splats there and that endurance block after the incline work was not particularly nice. Floor not too bad but wasn't happy with all the push-ups. I would give today a 2 (🪶🪶) out of 5 for gentleness. !<

On the treadmill we have four blocks. They all follow the same pattern - a minute push to buy-in, a base effort into a 30 second push and a 30 second all out. You then get some walking recovery before a final 30 second all out. In the first block the base and walking recovery are both 30 seconds, in the next this is a minute, then 90 seconds and in the last block it is a glorious 2 minutes. I had to get back to base in the later blocks as my heart rate would be in the grey but it was still quite nice to have a decent walking recovery. Good distance this morning of 5.01km (3.11 miles). \

2 blocks on the floor. The first is a circuit around your upper body. You start sitting on the bench with the hammer curls, maybe move to a lighter weight for the lateral raises, then the tricep extension and followed up by the sit-ups with a dumbbell on your chest. You have the option of a 300m row or just continuing on with the reps. \

Second block is much the same but this time it is lower body focused. You have the reverse lunge, step-out squats, a good morning followed by torso rotations. Again there is an optional row. Keep this up until your finisher - a minute of sit-up to torso rotation or your season of strength finisher. \
